title: Filter words through one rule object's bound reference

blocks.text: A **bound** reference (`rule::accepts`) fixes its receiver, so every call runs on that one object and can use its fields. A static method has no object and cannot read them.

items: `LengthRule(int min)` makes a rule with its own minimum length.

`boolean accepts(String word)` returns whether `word` is at least `min` characters long, counting every character, spaces included (so a rule of `0` accepts `""`). `null` is never accepted, through any of the methods below either.
`Predicate<String> asPredicate()` returns this rule's `accepts` as a predicate.
`List<String> keep(List<String> words)` returns the accepted words, in order.

blocks.text: A program may hold many rules at once, each with a different minimum.

cases.says: A rule accepts words at least its minimum long, as a method, as a predicate, and as a filter.
Two rules with different minimums judge independently; the minimum belongs to each object, not to the class.
A null word is rejected, not dereferenced.

concepts: A bound reference fixes its receiver, so every call runs on that one object and uses its state.
A static method cannot read an object's fields, so a per-object setting calls for a bound reference.
